title: "Order again" repeats the shop's most recently placed order (by when it was placed, never a draft) and builds the basket on the device, in the pieces that order carried, writing nothing until "Place order"
rootCause:
Both halves of the finding have one cause: "last" is read as "highest id", and the only server path that knows which order is last also writes a draft. The reviewer re-read every citation and re-ran the measurements on dos_qa; they hold.

1. WRONG BASKET: the server picks the highest id and counts drafts.
- `OrdersService.repeatLast` (backend/libs/core/src/modules/orders/orders.service.ts:172-218) selects `WHERE retailer_id = ? AND state <> 'cancelled' ORDER BY sales_orders.id DESC LIMIT 1` (:180-190).
- (a) Id order is not time order. Seeded ids are hash-shaped with the version nibble 7 (e.g. SO-0450 fb766131-c892-7c4b-…, SO-0281 ff9b5d1e-…). They sort randomly and above every real UUIDv7 (`01a0…`). Even a real client UUIDv7 is minted when the draft starts, not when the order is placed.
- Re-measured on dos_qa for ramesh.gupta's shop in each distributorship:

  | Distributor | Highest non-cancelled id (what repeats today) | Newest placed order |
  |---|---|---|
  | tarsun R-0001 | SO-0450 (delivered, 30 Jul, a rep's order) | SO-0912 (rep, submitted 13 Sep 06:33); SO-0885 (retailer_app, 12 Sep 18:43) when the finding was filed |
  | sai-distributors | SO-0281 (19 Aug) | SO-0428 (9 Sep) |
  | kalyan-agencies | SO-0035 (6 Aug) | SO-0182 (12 Sep) |

- (b) Only `cancelled` is excluded, so an unsent draft (a rep's, one left by smoke, or an earlier Order-again draft) counts as "the last order". All 9 drafts in dos_qa today are `salesperson` source. The apps already use another rule:
  - the rep app picks the first non-draft, non-cancelled row of `useShopOrders` (frontend/sales-app/src/lib/local.ts:471-477), ordered `_local_rev DESC, created_at DESC, id DESC` (:444-450), not by id;
  - the shop's Home list shows only placed states, sorted by `submittedAt ?? createdAt` (frontend/retailer-app/app/index.tsx:76-96).

2. A DRAFT ON EVERY TAP: the app calls a mutation before the shop confirms anything.
- Home's "Order again" (frontend/retailer-app/app/index.tsx:125-157) calls the MUTATION `orders.repeatLast`, which inserts a `sales_orders` draft plus lines (orders.service.ts:199-216, `insertDraft` + `writeLines`) before the shop has seen the basket.
- R7 then loads that draft through `?orderId=` (frontend/retailer-app/app/order.tsx:71-72, :124-141) and re-lines it with `orders.setLines` on Place order (:252-265, :290-293). Leaving R7 orphans the row.
- `useMutation` reuses the id and key only inside one mounted Home for the same input (frontend/libs/api-client/src/react/index.tsx:377-387). Any fresh mount mints a new draft.

3. WHY THE APP CANNOT FIX IT ALONE: no read answers "this shop's last placed order" by date.
- `orders.list` pages by `id DESC` (backend/libs/core/src/modules/orders/orders.internals.ts:315, :321; docs/23 §10 #8). That is why `GET /orders?limit=3` showed SO-0450 first.
- The real newest rows (UUIDv7 `01a0…`) fall below page one, so the device would have to page through the shop's whole history.

4. TWO TRAPS FOR A BASKET BUILT ON THE DEVICE (found in review; they constrain the fix, not the finding):
- (a) Pack size. `orders.create` re-derives pieces as `enteredQty × packSizeFor(unit, CURRENT case size)`, and `packSizeFor` treats `inner` as a case (backend/libs/core/src/modules/orders/pricing-lines.ts:94-95, :153-154). All 382 `inner` lines in dos_qa have pack_size_at_entry 12, below the current case size. Example: SO-0007's 3 inner = 36 pc would be re-written as 3 × 60 = 180 pc. Ramesh's Sai shop has inner lines in SO-0371 and SO-0387. A device copy that forwards the old `enteredQty`/`enteredUnit` would quote the old pieces on screen and place up to five times as many. Today's server copy has the same inflation.
- (b) Cache. `useQuery` serves a cached value for 30 s and shows a stale value while it revalidates (react/index.tsx:224-296; frontend/libs/api-client/src/cache.ts:138-141; `invalidate` keeps the data of a subscribed entry, :196-209). A seed taken from the first `data` of a shared key would repeat the order BEFORE the one the shop just placed.

The finding's suggested fix is right in direction but incomplete:
- Ordering by `created_at` alone still counts drafts.
- "Build the draft on the device" needs a server read that does not write, a pieces-preserving copy and a read that is never served from cache.

(2) Replace the `orders.get` seed query (:123-141) with `useQuery(['orders', 'last-placed', retailerId, repeat], () => api.api.orders.lastPlaced({ retailerId: retailerId ?? '' }), { enabled: signedIn && repeat !== null && retailerId !== null && seededFor !== repeat, staleTime: 0 })`. The key sits under `['orders']` and carries the nonce, so no cached or stale answer can seed a basket.
(3) Seed in an effect only when `seededFor !== repeat`, the read has data and `catalog.data !== undefined` (the current case size is needed). Each `item.lines` row becomes a NEW line `{ id: uuidv7(), variantId, qtyPcs: line.qtyPcs, ...entered }`. `entered` is exactly the case/piece conversion `setQty` already uses (:317-335), applied to `line.qtyPcs` with the CURRENT `byVariant.get(variantId)?.caseSize`: whole cases give `{ enteredQty: qtyPcs / caseSize, enteredUnit: 'case' }`, anything else (or an item not on the catalog page) gives `{ enteredQty: qtyPcs, enteredUnit: 'piece' }`. Extract that conversion into one local function that both `setQty` and the seed call. NEVER forward the old line's `enteredQty`/`enteredUnit`: `orders.create` re-derives pieces as enteredQty × case size with `inner` counted as a case (pricing-lines.ts:94-95, :153-154), so a forwarded inner line would place up to 5× the pieces the screen quoted. contractChange:
backend/libs/contracts/src/orders.ts gains one additive read, `orders.lastPlaced`:
- Route: GET /orders/last-placed.
- Input: { retailerId }.
- Output: { item: OrderDetail | null }.

No existing schema, input or output changes; `RepeatLastOrderInput` changes its doc comment only.

Why it cannot be avoided:
- "Built client-side until Place order" needs a server read that names the shop's newest placed order without writing.
- `orders.repeatLast` writes a draft by definition.
- `orders.list` orders by id (orders.internals.ts:321), so on seeded or imported rows the newest order is not on page one. Finding it on the device would mean paging the shop's whole history, which breaks docs/20.
- The guard builds its route map from the whole contract (tenant.guard.ts:276-285) and resolves the permission from the Nest handler that served the request (:288-295), so the new route is declared the moment it is in the contract.
permissionsChange:
Add `'orders.lastPlaced': ANY_MEMBER` to backend/libs/contracts/src/permissions.ts among the read rows, right after `'orders.list'` (:525).
- Same audience as `orders.get` and `orders.list`, which already return these rows. DOS-115 narrows only the five write rows and keeps the reads ANY_MEMBER.
- The retailer role is scoped by RLS (`tenantOrOwnRetailerPolicy`) and by `loadRetailer`'s link check (quote.service.ts:135-151).
- A salesperson gets only orders credited to it (the DOS-073 reach rule, applied in the query); the core spec pins it.
- No existing row changes. permissions.test.ts adds the path to the shop allow-list (:279-293). `describePermissionMatrix` in every service spec picks the new route up automatically.
migration: none. The query reads existing `sales_orders` columns under RLS. `sales_orders_retailer_idx (tenant_id, retailer_id, created_at)` (present in dos_qa) narrows to one shop's rows before the top-1 sort, so there is no new index and migration 0045 is not used.
decisionsNeeded:
Architect gate: this fix adds a contract procedure and a permission-matrix row.

1. HOW THE DEVICE LEARNS THE BASKET WITHOUT A WRITE.
   - (A, recommended) New additive read `orders.lastPlaced` (GET /orders/last-placed?retailerId → { item: OrderDetail | null }, ANY_MEMBER). `repeatLast` keeps its semantics with the corrected selection.
   - (B) Give `orders.list` date ordering (`coalesce(submitted_at, created_at) DESC, id DESC`) with a compound cursor; the app then calls `list({ retailerId, states: placed, limit: 1 })` + `orders.get`. This is docs/23 §10 #8 / DOS-009 (P2, lean mode): it changes the order and cursor meaning of every orders screen in seven apps and absorbs a P2 finding. Even if DOS-009 later lands, lastPlaced stays one indexed top-1 read with lines instead of two calls.
   - (C) Server-only: fix repeatLast's selection and keep the draft-on-tap. This leaves the finding's second half (an orphan draft per tap) open and contradicts its Expected.

2. WHICH TIME DECIDES "LAST".
   - (a, recommended) Placement time, `coalesce(submitted_at, created_at)`. It is exactly the Home list's sort (index.tsx:95). In dos_qa only 2 of 1,574 non-draft orders have no submitted_at.
   - (b) `created_at`, as the finding suggests. It differs only for a draft saved earlier and placed later.

3. WHOSE ORDERS COUNT.
   - (a, recommended) Any author and any source, as long as it was placed: rep, shop, phone, WhatsApp or van sale. Home's "Your last orders" and docs/06 "Reorder last order" both include rep orders. dos_qa placed sources: salesperson 1,217, van_sale 125, retailer_app 94, phone 41, whatsapp 35; ramesh's Kalyan shop has one van sale. On dos_qa today Tarsun would repeat SO-0912, a rep's order of 13 Sep.
   - (b) Only the shop's own `retailer_app` orders. The finding says "a different author", but its Expected says "the shop's most recent order (by date)".
   - (c) Any author, but not `van_sale` (goods sold off the van at the door).

4. SALESPERSON SCOPE.
   - (a, recommended) `lastPlaced` applies the DOS-073 reach rule (own orders only, like orders.get and orders.list), while `repeatLast` stays author-agnostic as today.
   - (b) Apply the reach rule to `repeatLast` too. That is a behaviour change outside this finding.

Record the choices in docs/22 §8.

tests.name: DOS-098: repeat-last copies the shop's most recently placed order, never a newer draft and never an older order with a higher id
DOS-098: GET /orders/last-placed answers the shop's newest placed order with its lines, writes nothing, and keeps a salesperson to its own orders

verify:
SETUP
- Services :3000-3007 and the retailer web app :5178 on dos_qa for the read-only steps; a copy of the current batch-2 test template for the writing steps (the walker). Restart the Metros with QA/tools/start-all.sh first (QA/STATE.md).
- dos_qa is rebuilt after DOS-032+059, which changes order numbers, so take the expected orders from SQL at verification time.

SQL A — the expected basket (first row per slug):
select t.slug, o.order_no, o.state, o.source, coalesce(o.submitted_at,o.created_at) placed_at, o.id
from retailer_links l
join users u on u.id=l.user_id
join tenants t on t.id=l.tenant_id
join sales_orders o on o.tenant_id=l.tenant_id and o.retailer_id=l.retailer_id
where u.username='ramesh.gupta' and l.status='active' and o.state not in ('draft','cancelled')
order by t.slug, coalesce(o.submitted_at,o.created_at) desc, o.id desc;
Then its lines: select v.name, l.qty_pcs, l.entered_qty, l.entered_unit from sales_order_lines l join product_variants v on v.id=l.variant_id where l.order_id=<id> order by l.line_no;

SQL B — the before-fix pick: the same join with `o.state <> 'cancelled' order by o.id desc limit 1` per slug.
- dos_qa on 13 Sep: tarsun SO-0450 (30 Jul, Godavari Table Butter ×40) where SQL A gives SO-0912 (Annapurna Sunflower Refined Oil 1 L pouch, 20 cs = 240 pc).
- sai-distributors: SO-0281 where SQL A gives SO-0428.
- kalyan-agencies: SO-0035 where SQL A gives SO-0182.

SQL C — every order row of the shop, any state (the fix must write none):
select count(*) from sales_orders o join tenants t on t.id=o.tenant_id
where t.slug='tarsun' and o.retailer_id=(select id from retailers where tenant_id=t.id and code='R-0001');

REGRESSION
- `pnpm smoke --run-tag <tag>` ends with 0 BROKEN (orders.repeatLast and orders.lastPlaced for every service that mounts orders; `--run-tag` because of DOS-160).
- Specs on a copy of the batch-2 template: `pnpm --filter @dos/core test -- src/modules/orders`, `pnpm --filter @dos/core test -- src/docs`, `pnpm --filter @dos/contracts test`, and every service spec (permission matrix).

risk:
1. repeatLast now repeats something different for every caller (smoke, docs examples, API users).
   - It repeats the newest PLACED order, never a draft.
   - A shop whose only non-cancelled orders are drafts now gets 404 "no order to repeat" instead of a copy of its draft.
   - examples.ts:1853-1856 and smoke's retailerWithHistory (smoke-endpoints.mts:275-280) pick a shop with delivered or closed orders, so docs and smoke still find rows.

2. The new static GET `/orders/last-placed` sits beside GET `/orders/{id}`.
   - It relies on find-my-way preferring the static segment, as `/claims/ageing` beside `/claims/{id}` already does.
   - If a mis-registered route ever sent it to `orders.get`, the answer would be a 400 on the id, never a data leak. The verify step checks both routes.

3. Quantities. The device copy keeps the PIECES of the repeated order and expresses them in whole cases where they divide, exactly as R7's stepper does. So:
   - an `inner` line comes back as pieces (the old unit is not reproducible on R7; DOS-101);
   - after a case-size change the shop gets the same pieces, not the same number of cases.
   Both differ from today's server copy, which multiplies the old entered quantity by the current case size (and inflates every seeded inner line). The on-screen quote equals the placed order by construction.

4. Merge conflicts on the same files.
   - order.tsx: DOS-074+097 (stock hint), DOS-096 (GST / You pay).
   - orders.ts and orders.spec.ts: DOS-003, DOS-004, DOS-096; orders.spec.ts tail also DOS-126 and DOS-115 describes.
   - orders.service.ts: DOS-115 (repeatLast's requireRole line), DOS-126 (confirmInTx), DOS-133.
   - permissions.ts / permissions.test.ts: DOS-115 (orders write rows, a test after the shop test), plus DOS-037, DOS-044, DOS-131+137, DOS-132, DOS-146 in other blocks.
   - smoke-endpoints.mts and examples.ts: DOS-115, DOS-116, DOS-037, DOS-044, DOS-131+137, DOS-132 in other cases.
   Implement on top of the merged held lanes and DOS-115.

5. The retailer app drops its `setLines` path.
   - A repeat draft left by an older build is still finishable: My orders → order detail → "Send this order".
   - Its `Repeat of <uuid>` note is still rendered by the `[id].tsx` marker (:348-355).

6. Visible residuals that are NOT regressions.
   - Home's "Your last orders" still sorts page one of an id-ordered `orders.list` (index.tsx:76-96), so its top row can differ from the basket Order again now repeats (tarsun: Home SO-0873, basket SO-0912). That is docs/23 §10 #8 / the DOS-009 class; the verifier must not file it against this fix.
   - R7 hides basket lines whose item is not on the current catalog page or search result, yet Place order sends them (order.tsx:338-342 vs :149). This predates the fix and applies to any basket.

7. Cost: one per-shop indexed top-1 read per tap replaces an INSERT of a draft plus its lines. Net lighter. The nonce leaves one small cache slot per visit, dropped by the next `['orders']` invalidation or on sign-out and distributor switch.
reviewNotes:
WHAT I CHANGED
